note: Smooth-scroll hijacker. window.scrollTo is intercepted, so the sweep must escalate to dispatched wheel events. Document coordinates may stay near zero, which switches ordering to checkpoint basis.
Transform-based virtual scroll. window.scrollY does not advance; content is translated. Geometry-based ordering is unreliable here by design.
Wraps content in a transformed container. Same failure shape as Locomotive.
Pinned sections make DOM order diverge sharply from reading order. Geometry-based ordering is required.
Animate-on-scroll: elements start at opacity 0 and are revealed by IntersectionObserver, which requires frame production.
Carousel slides beyond the first are often present but translated off-screen or display:none, so they land in the latent tier.
WebGL scene. Try runtime scene-graph introspection before rasterising anything.
Spline scenes are pure canvas. Text in them is usually geometry, not DOM, and often has no textual origin in the payload.
2D WebGL renderer. Text is drawn to a canvas and is invisible to any DOM walk.
Usually decorative. Lottie JSON can carry text layers, which the data-interception corpus will contain.
Shatters headings into per-character elements. Reassembly is mandatory or every headline becomes N single-letter blocks.
Client-side page transitions. Navigation does not produce a document load, so a fresh render per URL is required.
Hydration blob present. Useful as a corroboration corpus for canvas recovery; never as a content source.
Webflow interactions animate opacity and transform on scroll, so first-paint HTML understates the page.
Renders almost nothing server-side; a static fetch returns a shell.
